originalTitle: Why IBM shares crashed 26%: CEO Arvind Krishna highlights customer spending shifts towards AI
simplifiedContent: IBM's stock price dropped 26% because the company's quarterly results were not as good as expected. This happened because customers are changing how they spend their money, and they're now focusing more on artificial intelligence (AI). IBM's CEO, Arvind Krishna, said that customers are prioritizing AI and trying to get their hands on limited hardware. The company also had some internal issues and problems with its mainframe business, which contributed to the poor results. This matters because it shows that IBM is struggling to keep up with changes in the market and customer demands.

originalTitle: Fed's Warsh vows to 'do my job' if challenged by Trump
simplifiedContent: The person in charge of the Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, said he will do his job to control inflation, even if the President disagrees. This means he will try to keep prices from rising too quickly, and make decisions without being influenced by politics. Recently, inflation in the US slowed down a bit, but Warsh doesn't plan to lower interest rates right away. Because of this, investors don't think interest rates will go up soon, and are focused on Warsh's goal of keeping prices stable. This matters because the Federal Reserve's decisions can affect the overall economy and the stock market.

originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Wednesday
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market had a bad day, with the main indexes (Sensex and Nifty) falling by up to 0.7%. This happened because of increasing tensions in West Asia, which caused oil prices to rise and the value of the Indian rupee to fall. As a result, people are worried that inflation (prices of goods and services) might go up. This worry is stronger than the positive feelings about company earnings, which is why the market fell despite some technical signs that it should be stable. The geopolitical tensions are the main reason for the market's decline.

originalTitle: Multibagger Signature Global shares to be in focus on Wednesday after Q1 pre-sales rise 25% QoQ
simplifiedContent: Signature Global, a company listed on the stock market, will be closely watched on Wednesday due to its recent sales performance. The company's sales for the first quarter of the current financial year (Q1 FY27) were ₹1,970 crore, which is 25% lower than the same time last year but 25% higher than the previous quarter. This increase from the previous quarter is largely because of the launch of a new project called Tonino Lamborghini Residences. This news matters because it shows how the company's sales are doing, which can affect its stock price. As a result, investors will be paying attention to see how the market reacts to this update on Wednesday.

originalTitle: Gold, silver prices today: Comex gold and silver rebound as softer US inflation eases Fed rate hike fears
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: gold and silver prices went up on July 14th because inflation in the US wasn't as high as expected. This makes investors less worried that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates, which is good for gold and silver. As a result, gold futures reached $4,112 and silver reached $60. This matters because it shows that investors are feeling more positive about precious metals, especially with tensions rising in the Middle East. Overall, it's a good day for people who have invested in gold and silver.

originalTitle: Govt reviews fresh bids for IDBI Bank as stake sale process gathers pace
simplifiedContent: The Indian government and an insurance company called LIC are planning to sell a big part of their ownership in IDBI Bank. Together, they own almost 95% of the bank, and they want to sell about 60.72% of it. This sale will also give the buyer control over how the bank is run. The government owns about 30.48% of the bank, while LIC owns about 30.24%. This sale is moving forward, with the government now looking at new bids from potential buyers.
